pr_title: Adds support for reusing allocated timeseries for exemplar and samples.
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Harkishen Singh <harkishensingh@hotmail.com>

Fixes: #8787 

<!--
    Don't forget!
    
    - If the PR adds or changes a behaviour or fixes a bug of an exported API it would need a unit/e2e test.
    
    - Where possible use only exported APIs for tests to simplify the review and make it as close as possible to an actual library usage.
    
    - No tests are needed for internal implementation changes.
    
    - Performance improvements would need a benchmark test to prove it.
    
    - All exposed objects should have a comment.
    
    - All comments should start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
 -->

This PR allows shards to re-use pre-allocated `prompb.Timeseries` for incoming exemplars and buffer samples if they are already present in the queue, instead of creating another alloc of `prompb.Timeseries`.
pr_comments: When we buffer the samples, should I do a sort of existing samples in the slice based on time, before we push those samples to remote storage, or is it fine to not do any sorting?

I did the benchmarks and when the key is `uint64`, its lookup is faster, but still, the time taken is significantly higher than not having to look up at all, which I think is obvious.

If I make the pendingData as map, then the sorted order will no longer be true (and hence failing the benchmark).

I am not sure which direction to go or even if we should make this optimization or not, any advice?
Bumping into this during our bug scrub. @cstyan do you think the change in this PR is still relevant? Is this something we should shephard into merging, or should we rather close it?
I think this is likely still relevant. Even with cleaning up the series label cache more regularly, we're still allocating more memory and growing the heap more than expected.
Hitting this again during bug scrub. Since nothing happened in the last half year, we'll close this for now. But anybody who wants to pick this up, please re-open or create a new PR.

issue_context.title: group together samples and exemplars in a single TimeSeries proto
issue_context.body:
Remote Write is currently doing the easiest but least efficient thing, which is allocating a new `prompb.TimeSeries` per sample or exemplar that is buffered, even if some samples/exemplars share the same series labels, in which case they could be put in the same `prompb.TimeSeries` for the write request. 

Nothing in the protocol or proto definitions currently stop us from making this improvement.
comments: Also similar we could add for buffering samples together across series. As far as I can see: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/8fd73b1d281d3227c337b291e8c797a85251d3d5/storage/remote/queue_manager.go#L525 we only add one sample to each write request.

> we only add one sample to each write request.

From what I understand, we are only adding the sample to a local queue. The requests only triggers when we either reach the configured max number of samples in a request or we exceed the batch send deadline.

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/8fd73b1d281d3227c337b291e8c797a85251d3d5/storage/remote/queue_manager.go#L1055-L1127

I think the reason we do not group exemplar and samples in a single Timeseries is that WAL for exemplar is different than the WAL for samples. If we store exemplar in the same sample's WAL, this will be easier to handle (otherwise we would have to group and look back the samples queued and check of ref which will be expensive), given that both the WAL (exemplar and sample) have `ref` field.

Is there any reason why we didn't do that?

My guess is to keep WAL size reduced, but I don't think the increase will be significant.

@Harkishen-Singh IIRC one of the main reasons was that modification of an existing WAL record type, such as Samples records, would have broken forwards/backwards compatibility between versions without some kind of converter tool.

Assume any improvements made as part of resolving this issue can't make changes to the WAL format.

Hello from the bug scrub.

Nothing has moved here in the last 3y. We still think it's a valid idea, although we are not certain it will be a net win.
Maybe part of the overhead implied by this will already be done anyway in PRW2.0 as it has to create the symbol table.

Help still wanted. First step would be to do an MVP and benchmark it.

Yep, in the current version of rw2.0 we still duplicate the label symbol IDs since we create a `TimeSeries` proto per sample/exemplar/etc. but the overall problem is reduced a lot by using the symbols over strings. Still worth trying something here, but not an immediate priority.

review_comments: Since each shard will have its own series cache I don't think we need a mutex.
It would be really nice if we could use a ref for this instead of the labelString. Have you benchmarked this at all, I could imagine the lookups being fairly expensive, but could be wrong.
